newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asia LPG demand seen to hit 61 mln tonnes by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Asia LPG demand seen to hit 61 mln tonnes by 2000.

text.p: Asia's LPG demand is expected to reach 61 million tonnes by 2000, up 51 percent from 1995 levels, the LPG Centre of Japan said on Friday following a two-day regional seminar.

Total LPG output in 10 Asian countries -- China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Philippines, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam -- will grow to 32 million tonnes from 20 million over the same period, said Eisuke Yoshizaki, president of the center which sponsored the seminar.
The industry body came up with the estimates by compiling figures put together in each country and brought to the seminar by participants from the 10 countries.
They were mostly government officials in charge of energy policies, or officials for state-run oil concerns.
The widening gap between supply and demand in the 10-country area will boost LPG imports from outside the region by 42 percent from the 1995 level to 29 million tonnes by 2000, Yoshizaki said.
He said Middle Eastern countries will remain the major LPG suppliers for the region toward the turn of the century.
A surge in LPG demand in China and India is the major factor behind the tightening regional supply and demand balance, according to the data.

China is expected to become the largest LPG importer in the region after Japan by 2000, with the import volume in the year estimated at seven million tonnes, more than three times as large as the 1995 level.
India's imports are estimated to grow to 2.7 million tonnes by 2000 from 750,000 tonnes in 1995.
Malaysia, currently a net exporter, is expected to turn into a net importer by 2010 as domestic demand is forecast to surpass domestic production sometime between 2000 and 2010.
The export capacity of Indonesia, another LPG exporter in the region, is estimated to shrink to 753,000 tonnes by 2010 from 2.5 million tonnes in 1995.
